Ctx: ksctl > ksctl

Command line application for accessing a CipherTrust Manager.

Ctx: ksctl > Synopsis

This command line utility can be used to interface with a CipherTrust Manager system.

Configuration parameters can be used to pass in the username, URL, etc.
These parameters can be passed to the application in several ways.

When the configuration parameters are available from multiple sources,
the order of precedence (highest to lowest) is:

1. Command line arguments
2. Configuration file passed via the command line
3. Environmental variables
4. Configuration file in the default location

The parameters passed in as command line arguments override
everything else.

The structure of the configuration file must be based on
'config_example.yaml'. The name of the default configuration file is
'config.yaml'. It should be located in the '.ksctl' subdirectory of the
user's home directory.

On Linux, this file should be located in: '~/.ksctl/config.yaml'.

On Windows, this file should be located in: '%userprofile%:\.ksctl\config.yaml'.

If defined, proxy environment variables (i.e. 'http_proxy') will be honored
for all functions except 'init getpw'. 'init getpw' internally uses ssh
which means that ssh must be configured to be proxy aware for the users
local operating system.

Ctx: ksctl > Options

```
  --auth-domain string   The CipherTrust Manager domain where the user to be authenticated against.
  By default the auth domain is root or provide the domain where user created.
  --configfile string    Full path and name to a file that contains the
  configuration parameters (optional).
  Default for Linux '~/.ksctl/config.yaml' and for Windows '%userprofile%:.ksctl\config.yaml'
  --connection string    The friendly name of the user management connection you want to
  authenticate against. Default is local_account (default "local_account")
  --domain string   The CipherTrust Manager Domain that the command will operate in.
  Can be used only with user/password and not with token except 'tokens create' command.
  By default the command will operate in the root domain or the domain the user is logged-in.
  -h, --help   help for ksctl
  --jwt string  The JSON Web Token (JWT) - access token can be passed instead
  of user/password (optional). 'ksctl tokens
  create' creates a JWT.
  --nosslverify  Do not verify the certificate for SSL/HTTPS
  authentication (not recommended). Default is false
  --password string   CipherTrust Manager Server User Password. Do not use this flag to enter the password (masked) from terminal.
  --respfmt string  Response Output format (json is the only supported
  value at present, optional) (default "json")
  --server-name string   Name of the Server which is used to verify the hostname on the returned certificates unless nosslverify is given.
  --timeout int  Set time limit to wait for the response in seconds. Setting 0 will never timeout. Default is 0.
  --token string    The refresh token returned from the login command to be
  passed instead of user/password (optional).
  'ksctl login' creates a token and writes
  it to the config file.
  --trusted-ca-file string   Filename of the Trusted CA to be read from.
  --url string  CipherTrust Manager Server URL
  --user string  CipherTrust Manager Server User Name
  -v, --verbose    Provide verbose output while executing command
  (optional). Default is false
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms > ksctl alarms

Manage Alarms. List, state and clear commands.

Ctx: ksctl alarms > Synopsis

CipherTrust Manager alarms have a state (on, off, unknown) and a severity level. The severity levels are a subset of syslog severity levels; the supported levels are emerg, alert, crit, error, info.

Ctx: ksctl alarms acknowledge > ksctl alarms acknowledge

Acknowledge a CipherTrust Manager alarm.

Ctx: ksctl alarms acknowledge > Synopsis

Acknowledges an alarm by setting the properties acknowledgedAt to the current date and acknowledgedBy to this user.  The intention behind acknowledge is that when a user acknowledges an alarm it means that they are investigating the root cause.

```
ksctl alarms acknowledge [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms acknowledge > Examples

```
  ksctl alarms acknowledge -i id
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms acknowledge > Options

```
  -h, --help    help for acknowledge
  -i, --id string   Alarm id
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms clear > ksctl alarms clear

Clear a CipherTrust Manager alarm.

Ctx: ksctl alarms clear > Synopsis

Clears an alarm by setting the properites clearedAt to the current date, clearedBy to this user and state to off. The intention behind clear is that when a user clears an alarm it means that the alarm is no longer applicable, was determined not be an issue, etc.

```
ksctl alarms clear [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms clear > Examples

```
  ksctl alarms clear -i id
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms clear > Options

```
  -h, --help    help for clear
  -i, --id string   Alarm id
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms list > ksctl alarms list

List CipherTrust Manager alarms.

Ctx: ksctl alarms list > Synopsis

List some or all CipherTrust Manager alarms. Specifying an alarm name will return information on that alarm. Specifying an alarm id will return information on that alarm. Specifying a state (on, off) will return alarms in that state. Specifying the severity (emergency, alert, critical, etc.) will return alarms at that severity level.

```
ksctl alarms list [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms list > Examples

```
  Options:
    ksctl alarms list [-s <skip>] [-l <limit>] [-t <state>] [-n <name>] [-i <id>] [-e <severity>] [--source-type <source type>]
  ksctl alarms list
  ksctl alarms list -l 10
  ksctl alarms list -s 10 -l 10
  ksctl alarms list -t on
  ksctl alarms list -e critical
  ksctl alarms list -n 'NAE TLS Disabled'
```

Ctx: ksctl alarms list > Options

```
  -h, --help   help for list
  -i, --id string   Alarm id
  -l, --limit int   The maximum number of resources that can be returned by this query (optional) (default 10)
  -n, --name string   Alarm name (e.g. 'NAE TLS Disabled')
  -e, --severity string  Alarm severity (emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, info)
  -s, --skip int    The offset at which the search is started. Start with 0 initially, then use the limit value returned in this query for the next query (optional)
  --source-type string   Specifies the alarm configuration source type. Current valid values are 'server_record', and 'client_record'
  -t, --state string  Alarm state (on, off)
```

Ctx: ksctl backup browse > ksctl backup browse

browse resources inside domain scoped backup

Ctx: ksctl backup browse > Synopsis

This Operation lets you browse resources inside domain scoped backup that has been already browse prepared beforehand.

```

```

Ctx: ksctl backup browse > Examples

```
  ksctl backup browse --id <backup-id>
```

Ctx: ksctl backup browse > Options

```
  --filter string   A selection criteria to specify what type of resource to include in response. Only Keys resource type is supported. By default, no filter is applied and the response includes all the keys. Also, multiple filters are not allowed. Filter should be passed in JSON format containing the resource type and a resource query for attribute values to match. The resource query for keys supports the same attributes as the 'keys query' command's 'query' option. For example, to retrieve keys with a name containing 'mykeyname', set the filters to '{"resourceType": "Keys", "resourceQuery"  {"name":"*mykeyname*"}}'
  -h, --help   help for browse
  -i, --id string   Backup id.
  -l, --limit int   The maximum number of resources that can be returned by this query. (default 10)

The status of the asynchronous operation may be monitored via 'ksctl backup status' System backups can optionally be tied to a HSM when tied-to-hsm is specified. Backups tied to a HSM can only be restored on instances that use the same HSM partition. Do not specify tied-to-hsm if the backup is to be restored on instances that use different HSMs or for domain level backup. The backup is encrypted using the specified backup key id, or by the default key.
In case of Partial domain backup of keys, it is recommended to always backup all versions of keys.
WARNING: Taking backups of selective or only latest version of keys can lead to situation where data encrypted with non-backed up version is not possible to decrypt. To backup all versions of specific keys, use names. Sample request: "resourceQuery": {"names" : ["key1", "key2"]}

Ctx: ksctl backup upload > ksctl backup upload

Upload a backup file.

Ctx: ksctl backup upload > Synopsis

Upload a previously downloaded backup file. The upload file can be piped through stdin. Scope must be specified for domain-scoped backups. The whole file is uploaded by default. On slow connections, it is recommended that large backup files be uploaded in chunks. Because JWTs are limited to 5 minutes, any uploads that last longer cause the JWT to expire. A chunk size needs to be specified for chunked uploads. A chunk size of 10000000 bytes will prevent JWT expiration when the connection speed is 1 Megabit per second. An upload ID can be specified when starting an upload for a chunked request. This ID is assigned if not specified. If an upload is interrupted, to resume it, specify the upload ID that was used to start the upload. Information related to an interrupted upload can be obtained via the 'backup get' and 'backup list' commands. An interrupted upload can also be deleted using the 'backup delete' command.

```
ksctl backup upload [flags]
```

CCKM provides APIs for integrating as an External Key Store (XKS) Proxy service for Amazon Web Services.
Keys used for cryptography operations on AWS are sourced from managed Luna HSM connections.

Use the APIs in this section to:
  -Create, list, get, and remove external key stores.
  -Block and unblock access to external key stores.
  -Create, list, get, delete, and rotate credentials for external key stores.
  -Create, list, and get virtual keys and their versions, linked to a real key in Luna HSM.

  -Get CloudHSM clusters in the specified region that are not already associated with a CloudHSM key store.
In addition, APIs for AWS Key Management Service (KMS) to exercise are listed for reference.
These are APIs to encrypt, decrypt, and get key metadata for XKS keys, as well as to perform a health check on the keystore.

Ctx: ksctl cckm aws custom-key-stores create > ksctl cckm aws custom-key-stores create

Creates an AWS Custom Key Store (CKS).

Ctx: ksctl cckm aws custom-key-stores create > Synopsis

Creates an AWS Custom Key Store (CKS). Custom Key Store can be of type EXTERNAL_KEY_STORE or AWS_CLOUDHSM.
If creating a locally-hosted CKS, specify the following details:
  - Name of CKS
  - Region where the CKS needs to be created
  - AWS account to which CKS belongs to.
  - Luna HSM Partition ID
  - Linked state (false by default)
  - Blocked (false by default)
  - Source Key Tier (hsm-luna by default)
  - Enable MTLS (false by default)
If creating a CKS supported by an AWS CloudHSM, specify the following details:
  - Name of CKS
  - Kms where the CKS will be created under
  - Region where the CKS needs to be created
  - CloudHSM cluster ID
  - CloudHSM CU password
  - Trust anchor certificate
  - Custom Key Store Type ("AWS_CLOUDHSM" for CloudHSM key store)

Custom Key Store will be created with linked_state = false by default.
This means creating a CKS in CCKM doesn't trigger AWS KMS to create a new key store, and the new CKS won't synchronize with any key stores on AWS KMS until linked.

External Key Store will be created with enable_success_audit_event = false by default.
This means even if the CM feature flag FF_TOGGLE_XKS_AUDIT is on, there will be no server recording for AWS Custom Key Stores (Data Plane) APIs.

```
ksctl cckm aws custom-key-stores create [flags]
```

```

Synchronizes AWS keys. Specify the following details.

Ctx: ksctl cckm aws kms update-acls > ksctl cckm aws kms update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the AWS KMS.

Ctx: ksctl cckm aws kms update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the AWS KMS. User ID and group are mutually
exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an
existing action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupdate, and keyrotate. Now, to permit one more
action "keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly,
now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required    | Description
-------------------------------  |  ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create    |  keycreate  | Permission to create an AWS key.
Import    |  keymaterialimport   | Permission to import the key on the AWS KMS.
Delete key material  |  keymaterialdelete   | Permission to delete the imported key material from AWS KMS.
Rotate    |  keyrotate  | Permission to rotate the key on the AWS KMS.
Schedule Deletion  |  keydelete  | Permission for schedule deletion of the key.
Cancel delete  |  keycanceldelete  | Permission to cancel deletion of the key.
Synchronize    |  keysynchronize  | Permission to synchronize AWS keys.
Cancel    |  keysynchronize  | Permission to cancel a synchronization job.
Get Reports    |  getreports  | Permission to get reports.
Update key policy  |  keyupdate  | Permission to update the AWS key policy.
Update key description  |  keyupdate  | Permission to update the AWS key description.
Enable key  |  keyupdate  | Permission to enable the AWS key.
Disable key    |  keyupdate  | Permission to disable the AWS key.
Add tags  |  keyupdate  | Permission to add tags to the AWS key.
Remove tags    |  keyupdate  | Permission to remove tags from the AWS key.
Add alias   |  keyupdate  | Permission to add an alias to the AWS key.
Delete alias   |  keyupdate  | Permission to deletes alias from the AWS key.
Enable key rotation  |  keyupdate  | Permission to enable automatic key rotation of the AWS key.
Disable key rotation    |  keyupdate  | Permission to disables automatic key rotation of the AWS key.
Upload    |  keyupload  | Permission to upload the key to the AWS KMS.
List  |  viewnative  | Permission to view kms and its native keys.
List  |  viewbyok   | Permission to view kms and its external keys.
Get (AWS Keys)  |  view/viewnative/viewbyok  | Permission to get the details of an AWS key with the given id.
List AWS KMS   |  view/viewnative/viewbyok  | Permission to view kms and its keys.
Get (AWS Kms)  |  view/viewnative/viewbyok  | Permission to get the details of AWS KMS with the given id.
List (HYOK Key)    |  viewhyokkey    | Permission to view AWS HYOK keys.
Create (HYOK Key)  |  hyokkeycreate  | Permission to create an AWS HYOK key.
Block/Unblock (HYOK Key)  |  hyokkeyblockunblock   | Permission to block/unblock an AWS HYOK key.
Delete (HYOK Key)  |  hyokkeydelete  | Permission to delete an AWS HYOK key (applicable only to unlinked key).
Link (HYOK Key)    |  hyokkeylink    | Permission to link an HYOK key in CM to HYOK key in AWS.
List (CloudHSM Key)  |  viewcloudhsmkey  | Permission to view AWS CloudHSM keys.
Create (CloudHSM Key)   |  cloudhsmkeycreate   | Permission to create an AWS CloudHSM key.
Delete (CloudHSM Key)   |  cloudhsmkeydelete   | Permission to delete an AWS CloudHSM key.
List (Custom Key Store)   |  viewkeystore   | Permission to view Custom key stores.
Create (Custom Key Store)    |  keystoreadd    | Permission to add Custom key store.
Update (Custom Key Store)    |  keystoreupdate  | Permission to update Custom key store properties.
Delete (Custom Key Store)    |  keystoredelete  | Permission to delete Custom key store.
Block (Custom Key Store)  |  keystoreblock  | Permission to block any operations on keys in Custom key store.
Unblock (Custom Key Store)   |  keystoreunblock  | Permission to unblock operations on keys in Custom key store.
Connect (Custom Key Store)   |  keystoreconnect  | Permission to connect Custom key store to AWS.
Disconnect (Custom Key Store)    |  keystoredisconnect  | Permission to disconnect Custom key store from AWS.
Link (Custom Key Store)   |  keystorelink   | Permission to link Custom key store to AWS.
Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
Download Report    |  reportdownload  | Permission to download report
View Report    |  reportview  | Permission to view report content

```

```

Ctx: ksctl cckm azure vaults update-acls > ksctl cckm azure vaults update-acls

Grants permissions to users to perform specific actions on Azure key vaults.

Ctx: ksctl cckm azure vaults update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on Azure key vaults. User ID and group are mutually
exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing
action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupdate, and keypurge. Now, to permit one more action
"keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny
permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required  | Description
-----------------------------   |  --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create   |  keycreate    | Permission to create an Azure key.
Recover  |  keyrecover   | Permission to recover a soft-deleted Azure key.
Purge    |  keypurge  | Permission to permanently delete the Azure key.
Soft Delete   |  keydelete    | Permission to soft delete an Azure key from the vault.
Upload   |  keyupload    | Permission to upload the CipherTrust Manager key to Azure.
Synchronize   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to synchronize Azure keys.
Cancel   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to cancel the synchronization job.
Restore  |  keyrestore   | Permission to restore a backed up key to a vault.
Update   |  keyupdate    | Permission to updates the key attributes, tags and key operations.
List  |  view    | Permission to view vaults and its keys.
Get (Azure Keys)  |  view    | Permission to get the details of an Azure key with the given id.
List Vaults   |  view    | Permission to view vaults and its keys.
Get (Azure Vaults)  |  view    | Permission to get the details of the Azure vault with the given id.
Delete Backup  |  deletebackup   | Permission to deletes an Azure key and its versions from the CCKM
Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
Download Report   |  reportdownload    | Permission to download report
View Report   |  reportview   | Permission to view report content

```
ksctl cckm azure vaults update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm ekm > ksctl cckm ekm

Manage endpoints for Google EKM

Ctx: ksctl cckm ekm > Synopsis

Google EKM centralizes the management of key life cycle for various cloud services providers.
With Google EKM, you can use keys that you manage within CipherTrust Cloud Key Manager (CCKM) to protect
data within Google Cloud.
Google EKM feature provides access to an external key encryption key (KEK) for use as a wrapping key in
Google Cloud Platform (GCP). You can configure and manage policy , manage endpoints, and generate KEKs for
keys added to the key ring through GCP EKM. AES256 wrap/unwrap KEK allow users, developers, and organizations
to maintain separation between encrypted data at rest and encryption keys.

The benefits of using EKM includes following:
    Secure generation, storage and protection of your KEK on a root of trust configured in Ciphertrust.
    Privately maintained key provenance, managed access control, and centralized key management.
    Full life cycle management of your encryption key.
    Visibility for compliance.

Ctx: ksctl cckm external-cm domains update-acls > ksctl cckm external-cm domains update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the external cm domains.

Ctx: ksctl cckm external-cm domains update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the external cm domains. User ID and group are mutually exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, and refresh. Now, to permit one more action "keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required    | Description
-------------------------------  |  ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create    |  keycreate  | Permission to create an external cm key.
Update    |  keyupdate  | Permission to update an external cm key.
Delete    |  keydelete  | Permission for deletion of the key.
Refresh   |  refresh    | Permission to refresh external cm domain.
List  |  view  | Permission to view domains and its keys.
Get (external cm domain Keys)    |  view  | Permission to get the details of an external cm key with the given id.
List external cm domain   |  view  | Permission to view external cm domain and its keys.
Get (external cm domain)  |  view  | Permission to get the details of external cm domain with the given id.

```
ksctl cckm external-cm domains update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm google key-rings update-acls > ksctl cckm google key-rings update-acls

Grants permissions to users to perform specific actions on GCP key rings.

Ctx: ksctl cckm google key-rings update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on GCP Key Ring. User ID and group are mutually
exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing
action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupdate, and keypurge. Now, to permit one more action
"keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny
permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required  | Description
-----------------------------   |  --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create   |  keycreate    | Permission to create a GCP Key.
Synchronize   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to synchronize GCP keys.
Cancel   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to cancel the synchronization job.
Update   |  keyupdate    | Permission to updates the key attributes, tags and key operations.
Enable key    |  keyupdate    | Permission to enable the GCP key.
Disable key   |  keyupdate    | Permission to disable the GCP key.
Schedule Destroy  |  keydestroy   | Permission for schedule destroy of the key.
Cancel destroy    |  keycanceldestroy  | Permission to cancel destroy of the key.
Upload   |  keyupload    | Permission to upload the key to the GCP Key Ring.
List  |  view    | Permission to view key rings and its keys.
Get (GCP Keys)    |  view    | Permission to get the details of a GCP key with the given id.
List Key Ring  |  view    | Permission to view key rings and its keys.
Get (GCP Key Rings)    |  view    | Permission to get the details of the Key Rings with the given id.
Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
Download Report   |  reportdownload    | Permission to download report
View Report   |  reportview   | Permission to view report content

```
ksctl cckm google key-rings update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm google projects update-acls > ksctl cckm google projects update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the GCP Project.

Ctx: ksctl cckm google projects update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on Google Cloud project. User ID and group
are mutually exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an e
xisting action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions like cryptospacecreate, cryptospaceupdate, and
cryptospacedelete. Now, to permit one more action "cryptospaceblock" to the user or group, set "permit":true and
"actions": "cryptospaceblock" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny permission to the action
"cryptospacecreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "cryptospacecreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

APIs   |  Actions Required  | Description
--------------------------------- |  --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create Cryptospace  |  cryptospacecreate  | Permission to create a Google Cryptospace.
Update Cryptospace  |  cryptospaceupdate  | Permission to update the Google Cryptospace attributes.
Block Cryptospace   |  cryptospaceblock  | Permission to block operations on EKM endpoints in a Google Cryptospace.
Unblock Cryptospace  |  cryptospaceunblock    | Permission to unblock operations on EKM endpoints in a Google Cryptospace.
Delete Cryptospace  |  cryptospacedelete  | Permission to delete a Google Cryptospace.
List Cryptospaces   |  cryptospaceview   | Permission to view Google Cryptospaces.
Get Cryptospace  |  cryptospaceview   | Permission to get the details of a Google Cryptospace with the given id.
Enable Cryptospace EKM endpoints  |  cryptospaceekmenable  | Permission to enable operations on EKM endpoints in a Google Cryptospace.
Disable Cryptospace EKM endpoints |  cryptospaceekmdisable | Permission to disable operations on EKM endpoints in a Google Cryptospace.    hascustominit: true

```
ksctl cckm google projects update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm gws gmail wrap-private-key > ksctl cckm gws gmail wrap-private-key

Creates a wrapped private key

Ctx: ksctl cckm gws gmail wrap-private-key > Synopsis

Wraps a user’s private key. This API returns an opaque binary object (wrapped Private Key) that is sent as is in any subsequent Private key unwrapping operations.
This is a privileged operation, and will only be performed by authorized CCKM admins.
When wrapping a private key, you must specify any of the following fields along with optional field "perimeter ID":
- PEM encoded PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 (unencrypted) RSA Private Key. (Deprecated)
- PerimeterID is the perimeter ID to encrypt with the key. (optional field)
- Key ID of the RSA Private Key created on CM.
- Wrapping Key ID and Wrapped Custom Private Key where:
  - WrappingKeyID is the Key ID of the RSA key created on CM. It's public key is used for wrapping your custom PEM encoded PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 (unencrypted) RSA Private Key
  - WrappedCustomPrivateKey is wrapped custom PEM encoded PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 (unencrypted) RSA Private Key

```

```

Ctx: ksctl cckm gws issuer create > Synopsis

Creates a valid JWT issuer (third-party IDP). It validates authentication JWT created for wrap and unwrap APIs. When creating the issuer, you must specify a unique name for the issuer and any of the following combinations:

h: ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create
c:
Ctx: ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create > ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create

This will create a public, private RSA key pair in a given partition.

Ctx: ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create > Synopsis

This will create a public, private RSA key pair in a given partition. It supports four different mechanisms of the
key CKM_RSA_FIPS_186_3_AUX_PRIME_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_RSA_X9_31_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_RSA_FIPS_186_3_PRIME_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_RSA_PKCS_KEY_PAIR_GEN and
"CKM_EC_KEY_PAIR_GEN".

Create HSM Key is an asynchronous operation. Whenever the API is triggered, the status of the key will be
"in_progress" state. Users can check the status of the key by calling the get key API which will return the details
of the HSM luna key with the given id. Once the key-create operation is complete, the key status gets changed to 'AVAILABLE'.

```
ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create > Examples

```
  ksctl cckm hsm luna keys create --hsmluna-keycreate-params-jsonfile <hsmluna-keyscreate-params-jsonfile>
```

```
  --attribute-map-json-file string    attribute_map will be key-value pair of attributes.
  Example:
  {
    "CKA_EXTRACTABLE": true,
    "CKA_MODIFIABLE": false,
    "CKA_SENSITIVE": true,
    "CKA_ENCRYPT": true,
    "CKA_DECRYPT": true,
    "CKA_WRAP": true,
    "CKA_UNWRAP": true
  }

  --attributes string   Attributes of the key. Possible options:
  CKA_MODIFIABLE
  CKA_EXTRACTABLE
  CKA_SENSITIVE

  CKA_WRAP and CKA_UNWRAP

  Example: --attributes <attribute1,attribute2,...>
  --cckmPartition-id string  Slot id in which key would be created.

  Possible value includes: prime256v1, brainpoolP160r1, c2pnb163v1, secp256k1 and sect571r1

h: ksctl cckm hsm luna partitions update-acls
c:
Ctx: ksctl cckm hsm luna partitions update-acls > ksctl cckm hsm luna partitions update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the HSM LUNA partitions.

Ctx: ksctl cckm hsm luna partitions update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the HSM LUNA partitions. User ID and group
are mutually exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an
existing action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupdate, and keyrotate. Now, to permit one more
action "keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly,
now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required    | Description
-------------------------------  |  ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create    |  keycreate  | Permission to create an HSM LUNA key.
Replicate   |  keyreplicate   | Permission to replicate the key on the HSM Luna partitions.
Delete    |  keydelete  | Permission for deletion of the key.
Update    |  keyupdate  | Permission to update the key.
Refresh   |  refresh    | Permission to refresh HSM Luna partitions.
Synchronize    |  synchronize    | Permission to synchronize HSM Luna keys.
List  |  view  | Permission to view partition and its keys.
Get (HSM LUNA partition Keys)    |  view  | Permission to get the details of an HSM Luna key with the given id.
List HSM LUNA partition   |  view  | Permission to view kms and its keys.
Get (HSM LUNA partition)  |  view  | Permission to get the details of HSM LUNA partition with the given id.

```
ksctl cckm hsm luna partitions update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm microsoft dke endpoints create > Synopsis

Create DKE Endpoint for Microsoft Double Key Encryption service. You can create a new KEK or specify an existing KEK for getkey and decrypt operation. Existing KEK is applicable for migrating DKE integration from another CipherTrust Manager deployment.

```

Ctx: ksctl cckm microsoft dke endpoints create > Options

```
  --algorithm string  algorithm (optional)
   DKE Key Algorithm. Default is RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256.
   Options:
  - RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256
   Example: --algorithm RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256
  --auth-tenant-list string    List of IDs of auth_tenants for the DKE endpoint.
   Example: --auth-tenant-list <auth-tenant-list,...>
  --authorization-params-jsonfile string  authorization-params-jsonfile (required)
   DKE authorization parameters.
   Example: --authorization-params-jsonfile <DKE authorization params json file>
  --description string  description (Optional)
   Description for endpoint
   Example: --description <DKE description>
  --enable-success-audit-event  Enable or disable audit recording of successful operations on an endpoint. Default value is 'true'.
   It is recommended to turn it to 'false', if facing performance issue w.r.t. the data-plane APIs
   Example: --enable-success-audit-event=<false>
  --enabled  dke-enabled (optional)
   Example: --enabled=true
  --endpoint-create-params-jsonfile string   endpoint-create-params-jsonfile (optional)
   DKE endpoint create parameters.
   Example: --endpoint-create-params-jsonfile <DKE endpoint create params json file>
  --existing-key-id string  existing_key_id (optional)
   If source_key_tier is local, Identifier is to be used to find the latest version of an existing CipherTrust Manager key. This identifier can be the
   ID of any version or the name of a CipherTrust Manager key.  If the identifier is not supplied, a new CipherTrust Manager key will be created.
   This identifier is applicable to the migration of a DKE endpoint from one CipherTrust Manager deployment to another. When creating a new DKE
   endpoint using an existing CipherTrust Manager key in the new deployment, CCKM uses this identifier to associate all of the existing versions
   of a CipherTrust Manager key to the new endpoint.

   If source_key_tier is external-cm, Identifier should be of the external CipherTrust Manager(required).

   Source key must be an asymmetric key type, having Sign and Verify usage masks. In addition, this key must not be exportable or deletable.
   A DKE endpoint will be created using the latest version of this key.

   Example: --existing-key-id <existing source key ID>
  -h, --help  help for create
  --key-type string   key-type (optional)
   DKE Key type. Only asymmetric is supported now.
   Options:
  - asymmetric

  --key-uri-hostname string    dke-key-uri-hostname (Required)
   Base url hostname for KeyURI

  --source-key-tier string  Source key tier. Key source from where the key will be uploaded. Options are local and external-cm. Default value is local:

   - external-cm for External CipherTrust Manager.
   Example: --source-key-tier <source-key-tier>

Ctx: ksctl cckm oci issuers create > ksctl cckm oci issuers create

Creates a valid JWT issuer (third-party IDP). It validates authentication JWT created for health-check, encrypt and decrypt & get-metadata APIs. When creating the issuer, you must specify a unique name for the issuer and one of the following combinations
  issuer and jwksURI

```

   Example: --client-id <client-id>
  --client-secret string  Client secret of the CipherTrust Manager application as registered on third-party IDP.
   Example: --client-secret <client-secret>
  --create-issuer-json-file string  Paramaters for creating oci issuer.

  --issuer-name string    Unique name for the issuer.

Synchronizes OCI keys. Specify the following details.

```
  -h, --help  help for start
  --oci-vault string   When used with OCI key create.
  ID of the Vault to be used to create the key.
    When used with OCI sync start.
  ID of the vault from which keys will be synchronized. Provide resource ID or vaultID of the OCI vault.
  Multiple Vault ID can be passed as a comma seprated strings.
  Example: --oci-vault <oci-vault,...>
    When used with OCI report generate.
   Resource ID of the OCI vault on the CipherTrust Manager.
   Multiple vault id can be passed as a comma seprated strings.
   Example: --oci-vault <oci-vault,...>
    When used with OCI sync status.
  Filter the results of synchronization by oci-vault.
  --synchronize-all    For AWS cloud: Set true to synchronize all keys from all kms and regions.
    For azure cloud: Set true to synchronize all keys from all vaults.
    For Hsm Luna: Set true to synchronize/refresh all keys from all partitions.
    For SFDC: Set true to synchronize/refresh all certificates.
    Example: --synchronize-all=true or --synchronize-all=false
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm oci vaults update-acls > ksctl cckm oci vaults update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the OCI Vaults.

Ctx: ksctl cckm oci vaults update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the OCI Vaults. User ID and group are mutually
exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the
permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing
action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupload, and keypurge. Now, to permit one more action
"keyrestore" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keyrestore" and run the API. Similarly,
now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

 Apis  |  Actions Required  | Description
 -----------------------------   |  --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
 List  |  view    | Permission to view vaults and its keys.
 Create   |  keycreate    | Permission to create a OCI native key.
 Upload   |  keyupload    | Permission to upload the CipherTrust Manager key to OCI.
 Rotate   |  keyrotate    | Permission to rotate the key on the OCI KMS.
 Schedule Deletion  |  keydelete    | Permission for schedule deletion of the key.
 Cancel delete  |  keycanceldelete   | Permission to cancel deletion of the key.
 Restore  |  keyrestore   | Permission to restore a backed up key to a vault.
 Update(Edit key)  |  keyupdate    | Permission to updates the key like editing properties,
  |   | enable/disable key, editing tags
 Delete Backup  |  deletebackup   | Permission to delete backup of OCI key from the CCKM.
 Rotate to Native Key   |  keyrotatetonative  | Permission to rotate the key on OCI Vaults natively.
 Rotate to BYOK Key  |  keyrotatetobyok   | Permission to rotate the key on OCI Vaults BYOK.
 Synchronize   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to synchronize OCI keys.
 Cancel   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to cancel a synchronization job.
 Remove   |  keyremove    | Permission to remove a OCI key and its version
  |   | along with its backup from the CCKM.
 Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
 Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
 Download Report   |  reportdownload    | Permission to download report
 View Report   |  reportview   | Permission to view report content

```
ksctl cckm oci vaults update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start > ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start

Add an SFDC certificate synchronization job.

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start > Synopsis

Synchronize the SFDC certificates for the specified or all organizations.

```
ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start > Examples

```
  ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start --sfdc_organization_resource_ids bdf937f2-4f21-4ac1-a982-3dd81a28d7c8 --synchroniza_all false
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce certificates synchronization-jobs start > Options

```
  -h, --help    help for start
  --sfdc_organization_resource_ids string   Add a SFDC related entity using the SFDC organization resource IDs.
  Usage: --sfdc_organization_resource_ids <sfdc_organization_resource_ids>
  --synchronize-all  For AWS cloud: Set true to synchronize all keys from all kms and regions.
  For azure cloud: Set true to synchronize all keys from all vaults.
  For Hsm Luna: Set true to synchronize/refresh all keys from all partitions.
  For SFDC: Set true to synchronize/refresh all certificates.
  Example: --synchronize-all=true or --synchronize-all=false
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce organizations update-acls > ksctl cckm salesforce organizations update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the SFDC Organization.

Ctx: ksctl cckm salesforce organizations update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the SFDC Organization. User ID and group are mutually exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later,
for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate and keyrotate. Now, to permit one more action "keydelete" to the user or group, set "permit":true
and "actions": "keydelete" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required    | Description
-------------------------------  |  ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
Create    |  keycreate  | Permission to create SFDC keys.
Upload    |  keyrotatetobyok  | Permission to upload keys to SFDC.
Destroy key    |  keydestroynative    | Permission to destroy native SFDC keys.
Destroy key    |  keydestroybyok  | Permission to destroy BYOK SFDC keys.
Import    |  keyimportnative  | Permission to import a destroyed native SFDC keys.
Import    |  keyimportbyok  | Permission to import a destroyed byok SFDC keys.
Synchronize    |  keysynchronize  | Permission to synchronize SFDC keyss.
Cancel    |  keysynchronize  | Permission to cancel a synchronization job.
List  |  view  | Permission to view SFDC keys.
Get (SFDC Keys)    |  view  | Permission to get the details of an SFDC key with the given id.
List SFDC Organization  |  view  | Permission to view SFDC organizations.
Get (SFDC Organizations)  |  view  | Permission to get the details of SFDC Organization with given id.
Create cache only key endpoint   |  endpointcreate  | Permission to create cache only key endpoint.
Update cache only key endpoint   |  endpointupdate  | Permission to update cache only key endpoint.
Delete cache only key endpoint   |  endpointdelete  | Permission to delete cache only key endpoint.
Activate cache only key   |  cacheonlykeyactivate  | Permission to activate cache only key.
Upload cache only key   |  cacheonlykeyupload  | Permission to upload cache only key.
Update cache only key   |  cacheonlykeyupdate  | Permission to update cache only key.
Destroy cache only key  |  cacheonlykeydestroy   | Permission to destroy cache only key.
Create certificate  |  certificatecreate   | Permission to create certificate to be used to encrypt tenant secret.
Delete certificate  |  certificatedelete   | Permission to delete certificate.
Synchronize certificate   |  certificatesync  | Permission to synchronize certificate from SFDC to CM.
Delete Backup  |  deletebackupnative  | Permission to deletes a SFDC native key backup from CCKM.
Delete Backup  |  deletebackupbyok    | Permission to deletes a SFDC byok key backup from CCKM.
Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
Download Report    |  reportdownload  | Permission to download report
View Report    |  reportview  | Permission to view report content

```
ksctl cckm salesforce organizations update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl cckm sap-dc groups update-acls > ksctl cckm sap-dc groups update-acls

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the SAP Data Custodian groups.

Ctx: ksctl cckm sap-dc groups update-acls > Synopsis

Grants permissions to users or group to perform specific actions on the SAP Groups. User ID and group are mutually exclusive – specify either of the two.

For the first time users or group, actions are permitted as configured by the CCKM administrator. However, if the permissions of a user or group needs to be modified later, for example, a new action is to be permitted or an existing action is to be revoked, the CCKM administrator needs to set that particular action to true or false.

For example, a user or group is permitted actions, keycreate, keyupload, and keypurge. Now, to permit one more action "keyrestore" to the user or group, set "permit":true and "actions": "keyrestore" and run the API. Similarly, now to deny permission to the action "keycreate", set "permit":false, "actions": "keycreate", and run the API.

Actions Specification

The following table lists the accepted values:

Apis  |  Actions Required  | Description
-----------------------------   |  --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------
List  |  view    | Permission to view groups and its keys.
Create   |  keycreate    | Permission to create a SAP native key.
Upload   |  keyupload    | Permission to upload the CipherTrust Manager key to SAP.
Delete   |  keydelete    | Permission to delete SAP key.
Restore  |  keyrestore   | Permission to restore a backed up key to a group.
Update(Edit key)  |  keyupdate    | Permission to updates the key like editing properties, enable/disable key and enable/disable key version, and editing labels
Delete Backup  |  deletebackup   | Permission to delete backup of SAP key from the CCKM.
Rotate to Native Key   |  keyrotatetonative  | Permission to rotate the key on SAP Groups natively.
Rotate to BYOK Key  |  keyrotatetobyok   | Permission to rotate the key on SAP Groups using BYOK.
Synchronize   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to synchronize SAP keys.
Cancel   |  keysynchronize    | Permission to cancel a synchronization job.
Remove   |  keyremove    | Permission to remove a SAP key and its version along with its backup from the CCKM.
Create Report  |  reportcreate   | Permission to create report
Delete Report  |  reportdelete   | Permission to delete report
Download Report   |  reportdownload    | Permission to download report
View Report   |  reportview   | Permission to view report content

```
ksctl cckm sap-dc groups update-acls [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs > ksctl client-records alarm-configs

Manage Alarm processing configuration.

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs > Synopsis

When a new record is created on a node it is compared against an alarm config condition. When a condition is satisfied, check for the threshold in given interval of time period (if threshold is set to non-zero) and if it meets, an alarm is triggered on the node with the name, description, and severity from the alarm config and the details from the record. Multiple alarms may be triggered by a single record.

The config condition is defined using Open Policy Agent's query language Rego, https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/how-do-i-write-policies/.

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs create > ksctl client-records alarm-configs create

Create a CipherTrust Manager alarm config on client records.

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs create > Synopsis

Create an alarm config that is tested against any new client record on the node to determine if an alarm should be triggered. Refer to the parent commands help for a more detailed description of how alarms are triggered from records.

The config condition is defined using Open Policy Agent's query language Rego. The following example triggers an alarm when all the subconditions are true.

    'input.clientType == "CTE"; input.event == "VMD Shut down"'

```
ksctl client-records alarm-configs create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs create > Examples

```
  ksctl client-records alarm-configs create -n <name> -d <description> -e <severity> {-c <condition>|-f <file>}> -t <number> -p <seconds>
  ksctl client-records alarm-configs create -n 'VMD shut down' -d 'CTE event VMD shut down' -e critical -c 'input.clientType == "CTE"; input.event == "VMD Shut down"' -t 10 -p 1000
  ksctl client-records alarm-configs create -n 'VMD shut down' -d 'CTE event VMD shut down' -e critical -f condition.rego -t 10 -p 1000
```

Ctx: ksctl client-records alarm-configs create > Options

```
  -c, --condition string   A Rego query defined by Open Policy Agent. Separate subconditions by a ';'.
  -f, --conditionfile string   File with a Rego query defined by Open Policy Agent.
  -d, --description string  Description of alarm when triggered.
  -h, --help  help for create
  -p, --interval int  The interval is an integer value which defines the time interval in seconds and it is used for raising alarms if a threshold hits within this time interval.
  -n, --name string   Name of alarm when triggered (e.g. 'Weak RSA Key')
  -e, --severity string    Severity of alarm when triggered. See the REST API docs under Alarms for a list of severities.
  -t, --threshold int   The threshold is an integer value which defines the limit for raising alarm by observing the number of records fetched in given time interval. If it is not set then the default value will be 0 and it will not be used for raising alarm.
```

This function does all of the work to join a node to an existing cluster - must have a cluster already created.

Note: on a system with separate public [i.e. Internet-routable] IP addresses and private [i.e. NON-Internet-routable]
IP addresses, for example Amazon Web Services ["AWS"], the member and newnodehost flags must be internal while
newnodeurl and newnodepublic must be external.

```

Ctx: ksctl cluster fulljoin > Examples

```
  Options:

  ksctl cluster fulljoin -m <member-local-ip> -n <new-member-local-ip> -k <new-member-public-address> -f <new-member-config-file>

  ksctl cluster fulljoin -m <member-local-ip> -n <new-member-local-ip> -k <new-member-public-address> -f <new-member-config-file> -b -t 300
  ksctl cluster fulljoin -m <member-local-ip> -n <new-member-local-ip> -k <new-member-public-address> -p <password-new-node> -s <username-new-node> --newnodeurl <new-member-url> --yes -b
```

Ctx: ksctl cluster fulljoin > Options

```
  -b, --block    Block until the cluster fulljoin operation has finished (optional).

  -n, --newnodehost string  Host or IP of the node requesting to join the cluster.

Create a new azure connection. User has the option to upload external certificate for Azure Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option use_certificate and client_secret. Ctx: ksctl connectionmgmt ldap create > Options

```
  --base-dn string   Starting point to use when searching for LDAP users.
  --bind-dn string   Object which has permission to search under the root DN for LDAP users.
  --bind-password string  Password for the Bind DN object. Do not use this flag to enter the password (masked) from terminal.
  -q, --description string    Description.
  --early-listing-stop string  This parameter helps in enhancing performance of ldap users/groups browsing. When set to false, the entire list of users/groups that are present on the LDAP server is fetched.
  When the value is set to true, only limited number of users/groups are fetched from the LDAP server considering the "limit" specified by the user.
  To indicate that there are more number of users/groups present on the LDAP server to be fetched by the CM, "total" is shown as "-1". The default value of "early_listing_stop" is false.
  For example: If an LDAP server has 5000 users in total; and on CipherTrust Manager these params are set, "server_maximum_page_size" as 100, skip as 0 and limit as 1000 then number of entries in response will be returned as 1000 and total will be -1.
  When 'early_listing_stop' is set to false, CM will return correct total number of records which is 5000.
  --group-base-dn string  Starting point to use when searching for groups.
  --group-dn-attribute string  Attribute inside the group object which contains the group distinguished name.
  When this property is set, it uses the specified attribute to test for group equality. Example: dn, gidNumber.
  For example, if a groups's LDAP entry has "cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com" and the LDAP configuration has "group_dn_attribute" set to "dn", then LDAP user entry must have membership attribute exactly "cn=ship_crew,ou=people,dc=planetexpress,dc=com", in order for the user to be considered part of group.
  --group-id-attribute string  Attribute inside the group object which contains the group identifier (name).
  This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.
  --group-member-field string  Attribute inside the group object which contains group membership information, basically which users are members of the group. Example: member, memberUid.
  This value can be left empty to disable group support for this connection.
  --group-name-attribute string    Attribute inside the group object which contains the friendly name of the group.
  --group-search-filter string  Search filter for listing groups. Searching with this filter should only return groups.
  -h, --help    help for create
  --insecure-skip-verify  If true, skip the tls verification of a ca cert.
  --json-file string  Connection information passed in JSON format via a file. Parameters passed via the command line will override values in the JSON file. Eg: --json-file <filename>

  -n, --name string  Name of the connection.
  -p, --products string  list of products.
  --root-ca string   PEM encoded certificate used to determine if the server is trusted. Only
  applies if the server_url scheme is ldaps. If not provided, then the
  server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.
  See --root-cas-files to provide multiple certificates. Provide "" to
  clear the value when modifying a connection.
  --root-ca-files string  List of PEM encoded certificate files, separated by ';' on Windows, ':'
  on Unix like OSes, used to determine if the server is trusted. Only
  applies if the server_url scheme is ldaps. If not provided, then the
  server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.
  Provide "" to clear the value when modifying a connection.
  --search-filter string  LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in.
  --server-maximum-page-size int   This parameter sets the page size which determines the number of users/groups to be fetched from the LDAP server using pagination.
  By default 'server_maximum_page_size' is set to 1000, and therefore entries are retrieved from LDAP server through pagination. We recommend to ensure that server_maximum_page_size value is equal to LDAP server page size. To unset 'server_maximum_page_size', set its value to 0.
  Unsetting this parameter will disable the pagination. On disabling the pagination, it is recommended to use hard_limit parameter in the LDAP Browse APIs if there are large number of users/groups on the LDAP server.
  --server-url string  LDAP URL for your server. (e.g. ldap://172.16.2.2:3268)
  --user-dn-attribute string   Attribute inside the user object which contains the user distingushed name. If user_dn_field is not provided, an
  attempt is made to determine default value based on uid_field. Example: uid, dn. If uid_field is provided as sAMAccountName,
  Active Directory configuration is assumed and 'distingushedName' is used as default for user_dn_field.
  Otherwise, it will default to  'dn'. For example, if a user's LDAP entry has 'cn: John Doe' and this field is
  'cn', then the LDAP group entry must have a member attribute that is exactly 'John Doe', not 'cn=John Doe', in
  order for the user to be considered part of the group.
  --user-login-attribute string    Attribute inside the user object which contains the username used to login with.
  --user-member-field string   Attribute inside user object which contains user membership information, this gives details about group which user is member of. Example: memberOf, gidNumber. In case of user browsing, when both user_member_field and group_member_field are provided in the LDAP configuration then by default user_member_field will be chosen for browsing them.
```

Create a new salesforce connection. User has the option to upload external certificate for Salesforce Cloud connection. This option cannot be used with option use_certificate/regenerate-certificate and client_secret. User first has to generate a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) using "ksctl connectionmgmt connections csr --cn <common name> --csr-outfile <filename>". The generated CSR can be signed with any internal or external CA. The Certificate must have an RSA key strength of 1024, 2048 or 4096. User can also update the new external certificate in the existing connection. Any unused certificate will automatically deleted in 24 hours.

Manage SCP/SFTP Connections.

Ctx: ksctl connectionmgmt scp > Synopsis

The SCP connections menu can be used to configure SCP/SFTP connections. Supported auth methods for SCP/SFTP connections are key and password. For the auth method key, the user must download the public key from scp/public-key API and append it to the destination host machine's authorized keys. And for the auth method password user can provide the destination host machine password. User also need to provide host public key for verification, which can be located at "/etc/ssh/" at destination host machine.

  on Unix like OSes, used to determine if the server is trusted. Only
  applies if the server_url scheme is ldaps. If not provided, then the
  server's certificate is verified using the operating system's CAs.
  Provide "" to clear the value when modifying a connection.

Ctx: ksctl crypto encrypt > ksctl crypto encrypt

Encrypt data using the CipherTrust Manager's cryptographic keys.

Ctx: ksctl crypto encrypt > Synopsis

Encrypt data using the CipherTrust Manager's cryptographic keys.
This can be used to perform symmetric, AEAD or asymmetric encryption.
The key name needs to be specified.
The plaintext can be specified on the command line, or via a file.
For AEAD encryption (e.g. AES/GCM), the Additional Authentication Data (AAD) can be specified on the command line, or via a file.
The output is a JSON blob that contains the encrypted data and metadata related to the encrypt operation. The output is dumped to stdout, or written to a file on request.
For symmetric key encryption, the pad algorithm defaults to pkcs7, and the crypto mode defaults to gcm. An IV is generated if it is not specified (recommended). The default tag length is 12 bytes for AES-GCM operations.
For RSA key encryption, the pad algorithm defaults to oaep.

```
ksctl crypto encrypt [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl crypto encrypt > Examples

```
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -l <plaintext>
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -l <plaintext> -r <ciphertext-file>
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -l <plaintext> -a <aad>
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -n <plaintext-file> -d <aad-file>
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -k <key-version> -m <mode> -p <pad-mode> -i <iv-in-hex> -t 10 -l <plain-text>
  ksctl crypto encrypt -k <key-name> -l <plaintext> --nae-key-version-header
```

Ctx: ksctl crypto encrypt > Options

```
  -a, --aad string  AAD text string (this is the data that is authenticated by AEAD crypto). Use a file if the data is binary.
  -d, --aad-file string   File containing the additional authentication data (AAD).
  -r, --ciphertext-file string   File containing the ciphertext JSON blob. This blob is returned by the encrypt operation, and contains the ciphertext as well as metadata associated with the ciphertext. The blob is dumped to stdout if this file is not specified.
  -h, --help   help for encrypt
  -i, --iv string  The crypto Initialization Vector (IV). It is a hexadecimal string. An IV will be generated if it is not provided (recommended). Otherwise follow the security guidelines in "NIST SP800-38A" and "NIST SP800-38D" publications to ensure your IV construction is secure for CBC, CTR and GCM modes.
  --key-id string   The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.
  -k, --key-name string   The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.
  -e, --key-version int   This specifies the version number of the key used by the key operation. It defaults to 0. (default -1)
  --label string    A Base64-encoded string containing arbitrary data that will not be encrypted, but gives important context to the message. Used only with asymmetric RSA encryption and supported paddings are OAEP, OAEP256, OAEP384 and OAEP512.
  -m, --mode string  The crypto mode. Valid modes depend on the key type. TDES: cbc. AES: ecb, cbc, gcm and ctr.
  -o, --nae-key-version-header   This flag requests that the 3-byte NAE key-version header be prepended to the returned ciphertext.
  -p, --pad string  The crypto padding mode. Valid modes depend on the key type. Symmetric: none or pkcs7 (default pkcs7). RSA: pkcs1, oaep, oaep256, oaep384, oaep512 (default oaep).
  -l, --plaintext string  Text string that is to be encrypted. Use a file if the data is binary.
  -n, --plaintext-file string    The plaintext input/output file for encrypt/decrypt.
  -t, --tag-length int  The length of the AES-GCM tag in bytes (default is 12).
  --type string  Specify the type of the identifier specified
  by the 'id' option. Must be one of: name, id,
  uri, or alias.  If not specified, the type of the
  identifier is inferred.
```

The re-encrypt operation first decrypts the ciphertext with the original key and returns no plaintext, and then encrypts the plaintext with a different or the same key and returns the ciphertext.  For the Decrypt operation, the input must be the JSON blob generated as a output of the encrypt operation.  This operation doesn't return any plaintext as a output.
For Encrypt operation, The key name must be supplied, the Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) may be included for AES/GCM operation.
Optional information that are passed via json parameters include the key version, crypto mode, crypto padding mode, the Initialization Vector (IV), and the length of the AES-GCM tag. Ctx: ksctl crypto unhide > ksctl crypto unhide

Decrypt data using the CipherTrust Manager's cryptographic keys.

Ctx: ksctl crypto unhide > Synopsis

Decrypt data using the CipherTrust Manager's cryptographic keys. This is used to perform format preserving encryption.
The hide/unhide operations (FPE) use a default if no key is specified as a parameter, and will auto-create keys if a key name is specified that does not yet exist
The plaintext can be specified on the command line, or via a file.
For Unicode encryption (e.g. FPE/AES/UNICODE), the charset can be specified. This charset should be present on the server.
The output is a JSON blob that contains the encrypted data and metadata related to the unhide operation. The output is dumped to stdout, or written to a file on request.

```
ksctl crypto unhide [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl crypto unhide > Examples

```
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -l <plaintext>
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -c -n <plaintext-file>
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -i <iv> -l <plaintext>
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -c -e <keyversion> -l <plaintext>
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -c <charset> -l <plaintext>
  ksctl crypto unhide -k <key-name> -j <hint> -u <tweak> -w <tweakalg> -l <plaintext>
```

Ctx: ksctl crypto unhide > Options

```
  -s, --charset string  The charset used by the crypto operation. This charset should be present on the server. It is required for unicode hint.
  -r, --ciphertext-file string   File containing the ciphertext JSON blob. This blob is returned by the encrypt operation, and contains the ciphertext as well as metadata associated with the ciphertext. The blob is dumped to stdout if this file is not specified.
  -h, --help   help for unhide
  -j, --hint string  The hint used by the crypto operation. It is required for hide/unhide operations (FPE).
  -i, --iv string  The crypto Initialization Vector (IV). It is a hexadecimal string. An IV will be generated if it is not provided (recommended). Otherwise follow the security guidelines in "NIST SP800-38A" and "NIST SP800-38D" publications to ensure your IV construction is secure for CBC, CTR and GCM modes.
  --key-id string   The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.
  -k, --key-name string   The name, ID or URI of the key used by the crypto operation.
  -e, --key-version int   This specifies the version number of the key used by the key operation. It defaults to 0. (default -1)
  -l, --plaintext string  Text string that is to be encrypted. Use a file if the data is binary.
  -n, --plaintext-file string    The plaintext input/output file for encrypt/decrypt.

This operation creates a CTE ProcessSet.The parameters should be passed in as a json blob, either via the command line, or via a file.
Local flags hints:
  name (mandatory) : Name of the process set(string).
  description (optional) : Optional description of the process set(string).
  processes [array](optional) : Processes list which needs to be part of the process set(string).
    directory (optional) : Directory path of the process which shall be associated with the process-set(string).
    file (optional) : File name of the process which shall be associated with the process-set(string)
    signature (optional) : Signature-set ID or Name which shall be associated with the process-set(string)

The JSON string should be constructed per the schema in the API Guide (CTE/ProcessSets section, POST to /v1/transparent-encryption/processsets). JSON string example:
    {
  "name": "LinuxProcessSet",
  "description": "",
  "domain_id": "1001",
  "processes": [
  {
    "signature": "TestSignSet",
    "directory": "/home/testUser",
    "file": "*"
  },
  {
    "signature": "TestSignSet1",
    "directory": "/home/kyloTest",
    "file": "kylo.bin",
    "resource_set_id": "RS1"
  }
  ]
    }

This operation modifies a CTE ProcessSet.The parameters should be passed in as a json blob, either via the command line, or via a file.
Local flags hints:
  --process-set-identifier (mandatory) : Identifier for CTE ProcessSet. This can be UUID, URI or Name(string).
  description (optional) : Optional description of the process-set(string).
  processes [array](optional) : Processes list which needs to be part of the process-set(string).
    directory (optional) : Directory path of the process which shall be associated with the process-set(string).
    file (optional) : File name of the process which shall be associated with the process-set(string).
    signature (optional) : Signature-set ID or Name which shall be associated with the process-set(string).
    resource_set_id (optional) : Resource-set ID or Name which shall be associated with the process-set(string). It is used for ransomware clients as a resources exempt.

The JSON string should be constructed per the schema in the API Guide (CTE/ProcessSets section, PATCH to /v1/transparent-encryption/processsets/{id}).
 JSON string example:
    {
  "description": "",
  "processes": [
  {
    "signature": "TestSignSet",
    "directory": "/home/testUser",
    "file": "*"
  },
  {
    "signature": "TestSignSet1",
    "directory": "/home/kyloTest",
    "file": "kylo.bin",
    "resource_set_id": "RS1"
  }
  ]
    }

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers > ksctl data-protection containers

Execute container commands.

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers > Synopsis

Executes commands for managing containers.
A container is an object that contains all the information needed to access a piece of data. It can be a database or a file.
Supported container types are: DB2, ORACLE, MYSQL, HANA, CSV_FILE, FIXED_LENGTH_FILE.

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers create > ksctl data-protection containers create

Create a container.

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers create > Synopsis

This operation create a Container. The parameters should be passed in as a json blob, either via the command line, or via a file.
The JSON string should be constructed per the schema in the API Guide (Data Protection/Containers section, POST to /v1/data-protection/containers).
 JSON string example:
  {
    "name":   "Container1",
    "type":   "ORACLE",
    "username":  "Bob",
    "password":  "SuperSecret",
    "connection_url": "jdbc:oracle@test",
  }

```
ksctl data-protection containers create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers create > Examples

```
  ksctl data-protection containers create --name <name> --type <type> --username <username> --password <password> --driverclass <driverclass> --connection-url <connection-url>
  ksctl data-protection containers create --jsonfile <resource param file>
```

Ctx: ksctl data-protection containers create > Options

```
  --column-count int  Used with CSV_FILE and FIXED_LENGTH_FILE
  --column-position-info string   Used with FIXED_LENGTH_FILE
  --connection-url string  Database connection url
  --delimiter string  Used with CSV_FILE
  --driverclass string   Database driverclass
  --encoding string  Options are UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE, ASCII and ISO-8859-1.
  --filepath string  Used with CSV_FILE and FIXED_LENGTH_FILE
  --has-header-row string  Used with CSV_FILE and FIXED_LENGTH_FILE

  --jsonfile string  Parameters passed in JSON format via a file.
  --line-separator string  Used with FIXED_LENGTH_FILE
  --name string  Resource name
  --qualifier string  Used with CSV_FILE
  --record-length int    Used with FIXED_LENGTH_FILE
  --type string  Supported container types are DB2, ORACLE, MYSQL, HANA, CSV_FILE, FIXED_LENGTH_FILE.

 JSON string example:
  {
  "name": "Credit Card",
  "key_id": "a:b:c:d",
  "tweak": "1234567812345678"

  "character_set_id": "a:b:c:d"
  }

```

```

Ctx: ksctl data-protection protection-profiles create > Options

```
  --aad string  Additional Authentication Data
  --algorithm string   Resource algorithm
  --allow-single-char-input string   This option allows inputs with a length of 1 character to be tokenized.
  --allow-small-input string  This option allows inputs smaller than the recommended minimum size to be tokenized (4 characters). It is not recommended and can lead to security vulnerabilities.
  --auth-tag-length string  Authentication tag legth.
  --ca-list string  Used for sign and verify.
  --character-set-id string   The character set ID
  --copy-runt-data string   Enables null, empty and one character inputs to be passed through without an error. The token value returned is the original input value.
  --encoding string    Options are UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE, ASCII and ISO-8859-1.
  --format string  Options are LAST_FOUR, FIRST_SIX_LAST_FOUR, FIRST_SIX, FIRST_TWO_LAST_FOUR, NONE.
  -h, --help  help for create
  --iv string   Protection profile IV
  --jsonfile string    Parameters passed in JSON format via a file.
  --keep-left int  The number of characters to leave unencrypted starting from the left
  --keep-right int  The number of characters to leave unencrypted starting from the right
  --key-id string  The key ID
  --luhn-check string  To ensure token is luhn compliant.
  --md-name string  Options are SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512.
  --mgf-name string    Optional field. Options are MGF1.
  --name string    Resource name
  --p-src string   String in HEX format.
  --prefix string  An optional prefix to be added to all tokens.
  --salt-length int    Used in RSA with padding in local mode.
  --save-exceptions string  If used (for batches), does not throw an exception when an error occurs, else throws an exception on first error.
  --suffix string  An optional suffix to be added to all tokens.
  --tweak string   Protection profile tweak

Ctx: ksctl diskenc > ksctl diskenc

Disk encryption configuration, query and unlocking commands.

Ctx: ksctl diskenc > Synopsis

The disk encryption commands can be used for:
(a) creating a configuration file that can be passed to cloud init while
    launching the system
(b) determining if the disk is encrypted
(c) unlocking an encrypted disk.

The SSH key that is used while launching the system is also used for
unlocking the disk.

Unencrypting an encrypted disk is not supported.

Ctx: ksctl diskenc cryptsetup > ksctl diskenc cryptsetup

Configures an already running system for disk encryption.

Ctx: ksctl diskenc cryptsetup > Synopsis

This command configures an already running system for disk encryption.
After the system has been configured, it will start disk encryption on
next reboot.

If the disk is already encrypted, then it can be re-encrypted with a new
encryption key via '--reencrypt'.

The encrypted disk can be configured to unlock in one of two ways:
* Attended Boot (default) - Requires the user to explicitly issue the
  command 'secureboot' to unlock the encrypted disk. This mode provides the
  highest level of security.
* Unattended Boot - The encrypted disk is unlocked automatically by
  specifying '--attended-boot=false'. It is not recommended to use this
  mode because it significantly reduces the level of security provided by
  encrypting the disk.

```
ksctl diskenc cryptsetup [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl diskenc cryptsetup > Examples

```
  ksctl diskenc cryptsetup
  ksctl diskenc cryptsetup --reencrypt
  ksctl diskenc cryptsetup --attended-boot=false
```

Ctx: ksctl diskenc cryptsetup > Options

```
  -a, --attended-boot   Requires the user to explicitly issue the command 'secureboot' to unlock the encrypted disk. When the value is false then the encrypted disk is automatically unlocked during boot.
  (default true)
  -h, --help   help for cryptsetup
  -r, --reencrypt   Reencrypt using a new random master key. Valid only when the disk is already encrypted.

```

Create a new domain.
The domain name must be specified via the command line, or in the JSON file.
The list of domain administrators must also be specified via the command line, or in the JSON file.
The domain administrators are specified via a comma separated list of user IDs.
A JSON file specifying the domain creation parameters can be specified.
The command line parameters override the values in the JSON file.
The schema associated with the input parameters can be found in the API Guide ('Domains' section, POST to /v1/domains).
The JSON file should be constructed per that schema.
The JSON file can contain user-defined domain metadata (optional).

```
ksctl domains create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl hsm servers add > ksctl hsm servers add

Add a new HSM server.

Ctx: ksctl hsm servers add > Synopsis

Adds a new HSM server for high-availability (HA) and load balancing.

At present, this works for Luna Network HSM, Luna TCT HSMs, AWS cloud HSMs and nShield HSMs.

The parameters needed for adding the HSM can be provided via a JSON configuration string,
or as separate command line arguments.

The JSON keys associated with the configuration string for a Luna Network HSM are:
- "host" (this is a required parameter)
  IP or hostname
- "server-cert" (this is a required parameter)
  Server certificate in PEM format
- "serial" (this is a required parameter)
  Serial number of the partition to use, this is used to ensure the correct partition is added to the HA group
- "partition-identity-file" (this is an optional parameter)
  Partition identity file. Specify this parameter to use the STC protocol.
- "forceClear" (this is an optional parameter)
  When set to "true", forcefully clears all existing data on the partition of the joining node before adding to
  the HA group. Use with caution.
- "forceCopy" (this is an optional parameter)
  When set to "true", all existing objects on the joining partition are retained and propagated within the HA group. Use with caution.

The JSON keys associated with the configuration string for an AWS cloud HSM are:
- "host" (this is a required parameter)
  IP or hostname

The JSON keys associated with the configuration string for an nShield HSM are:
- "host" (this is a required parameter)
  IP Address of the Entrust nShield Connect Network HSM.
- "serial" (this is a required parameter)
  Electronic Serial Number (ESN) of the Entrust nShield Connect Network HSM.
- "hkneti" (this is a required parameter)
  Hash of the KNETI key nShield Connect Network HSM.

Luna Network HSM example of the JSON configuration string:
'{"host": "172.20.32.11", "serial": "1234", "server-cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"}'
nShield HSM example of the JSON configuration string:
'{"host": "172.20.32.11", "serial": "ABCD-02E0-D947", "hkneti": "4a2b4d660abc415654cd2b50a25dd38aafce8d60"}'
Example of the JSON configuration string for an AWS cloud HSM:
'{"host": "172.30.43.174"}'

Alternately, all these parameters can be passed in individually instead of via the configuration string.
Parameters passed individually override those passed via the configuration string.

```
