Ctx: ksctl key-policy > ksctl key-policy

Key Policy consists of all the permissions that is applied to a given label.

Ctx: ksctl key-policy > Synopsis

Key policy consists of all the permissions that is applied to a given label. In simple terms, it is the mapping of label to their permissions. These Permissions would be for clients, users and groups. It specifies which clients, users, or groups have permission to use the key, read key, sign key, etc. So, whenever an operation is performed on a key, all labels applied on this key are fetched. After that, all key policies related to these labels are computed which decides whether the client, user or a group is authorized to performed the operation or not.

Ctx: ksctl keys create > ksctl keys create

Create a key.

Ctx: ksctl keys create > Synopsis

This command can be used to create various managed objects: keys, certificates, etc. The key name, type, algorithm, etc., should be passed as command line parameters or via a JSON file.

************************************************************ CTE specific keys ***********************************************************************

   In order to use a key inside CTE policies, certain CTE specific attributes shall be specified in the meta of the key at the time of key creation.
   Here's an example request to create keys for CTE IDT policies:

   {
  "name": "CTEXTSKey",
  "algorithm": "aes",
  "size": 256,
  "undeletable": true,
  "unexportable": false,
  "meta": {
  "ownerId": "local|59ba6797-e5a6-4427-b11c-a5534b5a975e",
  "permissions": {
    "ExportKey": [
  "CTE Clients"
    ],
    "ReadKey": [
  "CTE Clients"
    ]
  },
  "cte": {
    "persistent_on_client": true,
    "encryption_mode": "XTS",
    "cte_versioned": false
  }
  },
  "xts": true,
  "id": "95cc7868-89bf-492b-b868-bbb884a9b379"
   }

   CTE specific parameters which shall be supplied in the meta field at the time of key creation are mentioned below.

   parent-parameter | parameter | description
   --- | --- | ---
   meta | permissions | "ExportKey" and "ReadKey" are required for group "CTE Clients".
   cte (inside meta) | persistent_on_client | true or false
   cte (inside meta) | encryption_mode | Mode can be either CBC, CBC_CS1 or XTS. CBC_CS1 and XTS can be supplied only when "xts" parameter of key creation request is true
   cte (inside meta) | cte_versioned | true or false. true will be applicable for keys to be used in LDT policies, for rest of the policies it shall remain false
    - | unexportable | false. It should always be false in order to consume this key for CTE policies
    - | xts | true or false. For usecases like IDT, device level protection using Standard CTE policy and for COS policies, xts flag shall be marked as true

  ***************************************************************************************************************************************************

  ********************************************** Creating Keys Using Templates **********************************************************************
    Keys can be created using templates by providing the template id in request. The key parameters which are present in template will be used to
    create key. The users can also provide request parameters along with template id.
    The parameters from request or template takes priority based on access level.
  For privileged users like ( users in Key Users / Key Admins / Admins  group), the precedence is for request parameters if same parameters are
  coming from templates as well. The different parameters will be merged .
  For Restricted users ( users in Restricted Key Users group), the precedence is for template parameters. The different parameters will be merged.
  There is allowed list of key parameters for restricted users which can be provided in request.
   - name
   - description
   - labels
   - aliases
   - Material
   - Password
  For Restricted users, ownerId in template key_attributes meta needs to same as given in request params meta.
  ****************************************************************************************************************************************************

```

```

Ctx: ksctl keys query > ksctl keys query

Complex query for a key.

Ctx: ksctl keys query > Synopsis

This can be used to construct complex queries for locating keys. The query parameters should be passed in as a JSON blob, either via the command line, or via a file. The schema associated with the query parameters can be found in the API Guide ('Keys' command, POST to /v1/vault/query-keys). Some of the JSON key/value pairs are discussed next:
- skip (integer): The index of the first resource to return. Equivalent to 'offset' in SQL. Defaults to 0.
- limit (integer): The max number of resources to return. Equivalent to 'limit' in SQL. Defaults to 10.
- returnOnlyIDs (boolean): If not specified (or false), all key information is returned. If set to true, just the key IDs are returned.
- name (string): Filter by name. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.
- names (array of string): A set of names of keys that filters results to those with matching names.
- id (string): Find the key with a matching ID.
- uri (string): Filter by URI. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.
- version (integer): Filter by key version. All key versions are returned if this is not specified. The latest key is returned if version is specified as -1.
- algorithm (string): Filter by key algorithm.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.
- size (integer): Find keys with matching size.
- curveids (array of string): Filter by elliptic key curve id.  Results will match *any* of the values.
- states (array of string): Filter by one or more key states. Allowed values are "Pre-Active", "Active", "Deactivated", "Destroyed", "Compromised" and "Destroyed Compromised".
- aliases (array of string): Filter by alias. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used when a single alias is specified.
- linkTypes (array of string): Filter by link type. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used when a single link type is specified. See the links documentation for the various link types.
- usageMask (integer): Filters by cryptographic usage mask. See the keys documentation for valid values.
- metaContains (json serialized blob as string): Filter contents in key metadata. See API playground documentation for examples of JSON containment.
- objectTypes (array of string): Filter by KMIP object types. The '?' and '*' wildcard characters or comma may be used when a single object type is specified. Valid object types are: "Certificate", "Symmetric Key", "Public Key", "Private Key", "Split Key", "Secret Data", "Opaque Object".
- sha1Fingerprint (string): Filters results to those with matching SHA1 fingerprints.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used. This fingerprint is truncated and is based on the first 8 bytes of the SHA1 checksum. To be backward compatible with 'KeySecure Classic', it is based on ASN.1 representation of PKCS#1 public key.
- sha256Fingerprint (string): Filters results to those with matching SHA256 fingerprints.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used.
- sha384Fingerprints (array of string): Filters results to those with matching SHA384 fingerprints.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used. You can use an empty value [""] to search keys with no sha384Fingerprint.
- cteKeyHash (array of string): Filters results to those with matching cte key hash.  The '?' and '*' wildcard characters may be used. You can use an empty value [""] to search keys with no cteKeyHash.

- keyCheckValues (array of string): Filters results based on the matching Key Check Values (KCVs). You can use an empty value [""] to search keys with no KCV.
- createdBefore (RFC3339Nano date-time): Find keys created before the specified timestamp. Timestamp example: 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z
- createdAfter (RFC3339Nano date-time): Find keys created after the specified timestamp.
- certFields: Search for keys containing the specified certificate attributes. Refer to the API guide for further details.
- rotationDateReached (boolean): If set to true, returns keys with rotation date/time less than or equals to current date/time. If set to false, returns keys with rotation date/time greater than current date/time.
- compareIDWithUUID (string): If "compare-id-with-uuid" is set to "equal", then it returns keys whose IDs are equal to their UUIDs. If "compare-id-with-uuid" is set to "notequal", then it returns keys whose IDs are not equal to their UUIDs. The supported values are "equal" and "notequal".
- labels (string): Find keys that match label selector expressions. Multiple values are logically ANDed.
  - Select keys that have the label {"region": "noram"}:
  [ "region=noram" ]
  - Select keys that do not have the label {"region": "noram"}:
  [ "region!=noram" ]
  - Select keys that have either {"region": "noram"} or {"region": "emea"}
  [ "region in (noram,emea)" ]
  - Select keys that do not have {"region": "noram"} nor {"region": "emea"}
  [ "region notin (noram,emea)" ]
  - Select keys that have the label key region (the value may be anything)
  [ "region" ]
  - Select keys that not have the label key region
  [ "!region" ]
- permissions (array of string): Filter by permissions, The filter returns only those keys on which the user performing the query has the same permissions as given in the query. The permissions are given to a group in the key meta and the group must have the "ReadKey" permission. The user performing the query must be a member of the group having those permissions. Allowed values are "EncryptWithKey", "DecryptWithKey", "MACWithKey", "MACVerifyWithKey", "SignWithKey", "SignVerifyWithKey", "ReadKey", "UseKey", and "ExportKey".

JSON string examples:

  {
    "limit": 10,
    "name": "keyname*",
    "version": "-1",
    "algorithm": "AE*",
    "size": 256,
    "curveids": [ "secp224k1",	"secp256k1" ],
    "states": [ "Pre-Active", "Active" ],
    "aliases": [ "alias*" ],
    "linkTypes": [ "privateKey", "publicKey" ],
    "usageMask": 3,
    "metaContains": "{\"color\": \"yellow\"}",
    "objectTypes": [ "Symmetric Key",	"Public Key" ],
    "sha1Fingerprint": "b1e9364f06db9928",
    "sha256Fingerprint": "f445801e0cb899262c9b9e219836880d73ca2d1b0b9c15fb959c90eb121234e3",
    "createdBefore": "2018-11-28T23:59:59Z",
    "createdAfter": "2018-11-28T00:00:00Z",
    "compareIDWithUUID": "equal",
    "labels": [ "region=noram", "team!=sales" ]
  }

  { "certFields": { "certType": "x509-der"}, "returnOnlyIDs": true, "rotationDateReached": true }

  { "permissions": ["ReadKey","UseKey"] }

```

Ctx: ksctl keys revoke > ksctl keys revoke

Revokes a key, marking it deactivated or compromised.

Ctx: ksctl keys revoke > Synopsis

Transitions the key to the Deactivated, Compromised, or CompromisedDestroyed
state.  If the key is revoked with a reason of CACompromised or
KeyCompromised, the key will transition to either Compromised or
CompromisedDestroyed state.  All other reasons transition the key
to the Deactivated state.

If the key transitions to the Deactivated state, the deactivationDate will
be set to the current time.

If the key transitions to the Compromised or CompromisedDestroyed state,
the compromiseDate will be set to the current time, and the
compromiseOccurrenceDate will be set to either the specified time, or
to the creation time of the key.

The revocation reason must be specified. Other parameters are optional.

An error will be returned if the key is not found, the reason is
invalid, the key is archived, or the key is not able to transition to
the required state.

```

  -l, --limit int    The maximum number of connection information structures that can be returned by this query.
  --root-ca string   Optional list of certificates that are used to determine if the server is trusted.

  --search-filter string  LDAP search filter which can further restrict the set of users who will be allowed to log in.

Ctx: ksctl migration-split-keys > ksctl migration-split-keys

Manage split keys used for migrating backups from a DSM.

Ctx: ksctl migration-split-keys > Synopsis

Manage split keys used for migrating backups from a DSM (Data Security Management) box.
These keys are split keys. That is, a single key is split into many shares.
A minimum number of shares is required to reassemble the key, this number is referred to as the threshold.
The APIs in this section can be used for CRUD operations on these keys.
The APIs also provide methods for adding, modifying and deleting shares associated with these keys.

The DSM uses these type of keys for protecting its exported backups.
The CipherTrust Manager uses these keys for decrypting backups uploaded from the DSM.

Ctx: ksctl migrations apply > ksctl migrations apply

Migrate the specified backup file to a CipherTrust Manager.

Ctx: ksctl migrations apply > Synopsis

Use this command to migrate a specific backup file to a
CipherTrust Manager.

This command starts an asynchronous operation that restores a KeySecure
Classic or Vormetric DSM backup file. Only one migration can run at a time.

The status of the asynchronous operation may be monitored via
'ksctl migrations status'.

Allowed values for users type are 'local' and 'ldap', default being
'local'. If users type is 'ldap' then the parameter 'ldap-conn-name' is
required.

```

```

Ctx: ksctl migrations apply > Examples

```
  ksctl migrations apply --id <id> --migpassword <password>
  ksctl migrations apply -i <id> -p <password>
  ksctl migrations apply -i <id> -p <password> -e <users-type> -n <ldap-conn-name>
  ksctl migrations apply --id <id> [--private-key-id <private-key-id>]  [--group-name <group-name>] [--domains <domains>] [--containers <containerIDs>] [--auto-cte-groups] [--migrateCCKMSourceKeys]
  ksctl migrations apply -i <id> -p <password> -e <users-type> -n <ldap-conn-name> [--domains <domains>] [--key-owners-jsonfile <json-file>]
  ksctl migrations apply --id <id> [--private-key-id <private-key-id>] [--externalcm-domain-id <externalcm-domain-id>] [--externalcm-connection <externalcm-connection>] [--migrate-dke-source-keys]
  ksctl migrations apply --id <id> [--migrate-dsmkeys-to-externalcm-from-cm]
  ksctl migrations apply --id <id> [--update-cloudkeys-with-externalcm-keys]
```

Ctx: ksctl migrations apply > Options

```
  --auto-cte-groups  This optional parameter is applicable to DSM migrations.
  It can be used to control how CTE keys get migrated.
  On the DSM, if a key has the "Source" field set to "From DSM" or an
  empty string, and this flag is set to true, the key is migrated so that
  it is fully accessible to members of the "CTE Clients" group.

  --containers string  This optional parameter is applicable to CCKM Enterprise migrations. Specify the IDs of Azure/AWS/Salesforce containers to be migrated.
  If this parameter is not specified, all Azure/AWS/Salesforce containers will be migrated. To specify multiple containers, enter their IDs separated by commas.
  Example: --containers "<container1-id>,<container2-id>,...,<containerN-id>"

  --domains string   This optional parameter is applicable to DSM migrations.
  All domains are migrated if this is not specified.
  It can contain a comma separated list of DSM domain names, only those domains are migrated.

  --externalcm-connection string   This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
  It is used to provide the connection name of the external CM from which the keys are to be migrated.

  --externalcm-domain-id string    This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
  It is used to provide the domain name which belongs the external CM, where the keys are to be migrated.

  --group-name string  This optional parameter is applicable to DSM migrations.
  It can be used to specify the name of a key-sharing group.
  This group is created in all the domains that are migrated.
  The keys in the migrated domains will be accessible to all the members of this group.

  -h, --help    help for apply
  -i, --id string    The migration backup file ID.
  --key-owners stringArray    This parameter contains the key-value pairs.
  The key corresponds to the domain in the DSM backup and the value is the user id of an existing user in the root domain of the CipherTrust Manager.
  This argument can be repeated multiple time to provide multiple values, for example:
  --key-owners "newdom1:local|f02c1025-b659-4b96-816c-d770e0eaab46" --key-owners "newdom2:local|f02c1025-b659-4b96-816c-d770e0eaab46"
  Note:- No space should be provided between domain and userID <domain:userID>

  --key-owners-jsonfile string  Name of file containing JSON serialized domain and corresponding user id.
  The JSON file should be constructed as per the schema specified in the API Guide ('Migrations' section, POST to v1/migrations/{id}/migrate).

  -n, --ldap-conn-name string  Applicable to 'KeySecure Classic' migrations.
  Required if the users-type is ldap, should specify name of the LDAP connection being migrated.

  -p, --migpassword string    Password needed for decrypting the KeySecure Classic backup file.
  --migrate-cckm-source-keys  This optional parameter is only applicable for cckm migration.
  If it's set to true, the source key created in DSM from CCKM appliance will be migrated to CM.

  --migrate-cloudkeys-with-externalcm   This optional parameter is only applicable for cckm migration while migrating cloud keys created in CCKM Enterprise..
  If this flag is set to true, the cloud key created in CCKM enterprise will be migrated to CipherTrust Manager if DSM source keys migration done.

  --migrate-dke-source-keys   This is an optional parameter & is only used while migrating CCKM DKE Keys.
  If this flag is set to true, the CCKM DKE Keys will be migrated to external CipherTrust Manager.

  --migrate-dsmkeys-to-externalcm-from-cm   This optional parameter used only while migrating source keys from DSM to External CipherTrust Manager
  when the cloud keys from CCKM Enterprise are already migrated to CipherTrust Manager.
  If this flag is set to true, the source keys from DSM to External CipherTrust Manager will be migrated.

  --migrate-only-cckm-source-keys  This optional parameter is only applicable for cckm migration while migrating DSM source keys created in CCKM Enterprise.
  If this flag is set to true, the key created in DSM from CCKM enterprise will be migrated to CipherTrust Manager.

  --private-key-id string  It specifies the name or id of the CM private key. It is required only for the cckm product.

  --update-cloudkeys-with-externalcm-keys   This is an optional parameter.
  Use this flag to update linking of cloud keys with DSM as keysource to External CM. If this flag is set to true,
  The source keys of the cloud keys will be updated with the corresponding migrated External CipherTrust Manager key.

  -e, --users-type string  Required for 'KeySecure Classic' migrations.
  Specifies type of user accounts being migrated, valid values are 'local', 'ldap'.

```

Ctx: ksctl migrations upload > ksctl migrations upload

Upload a migration backup file.

Ctx: ksctl migrations upload > Synopsis

Use this command to upload a migration backup file to a CipherTrust Manager.

If the file name is not specified, the program reads the data to be uploaded from stdin.

An optional description, and an optional password hint, may be specified.
They are stored alongside the file as metadata. The ID returned by this
command is used for identifying the file in other commands.

On slow connections, it is recommended that large backup files be uploaded
in chunks. This is because JWTs have a limited duration (5 minutes), any
uploads that last longer cause the JWT to expire. A chunk size needs to be
specified for chunked uploads. A chunk size of 10000000 bytes will prevent
JWT expiration when the connection speed is 1 Megabit per second.

An upload ID may be specified when starting an upload, it is assigned if
not specified. The upload ID that was used while starting an upload should
be specified in order to resume an interrupted upload.

Information related to an interrupted upload can be obtained via the
'migrations get' and 'migrations list' commands.

An interrupted upload can be deleted using the 'migrations delete' command.

```
ksctl migrations upload [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl migrations upload > Examples

```
  Options:
    ksctl migrations upload [--file <migration-backup-file>] [--desc <file-description>] [--hint <password-hint>] [--chunk-size <chunk-size>] [--upload-id <upload-id>] [--checksum <sha256-sum>]
  ksctl migrations upload
  ksctl migrations upload --file <migration-backup-file>
  ksctl migrations upload --file <migration-backup-file> --desc <file-description> --hint <password-hint>
  ksctl migrations upload --file <migration-backup-file> --checksum <sha256-sum>
  ksctl migrations upload --file <migration-backup-file> --chunk-size 10000000
  ksctl migrations upload --file <migration-backup-file> --chunk-size 10000000 --upload-id <upload-id> --checksum <sha256-sum>
```

Ctx: ksctl migrations upload > Options

```
  -w, --checksum string    SHA256 checksum of file that is uploaded. If specified, the sha256 checksum of the uploaded file will be validated using this value.
  -c, --chunk-size int  Upload chunk size in bytes. Useful when uploading large backup files.
  -d, --desc string    Description of the migration backup file.
  -f, --file string    Set the migration backup file name. The data to upload is read from this file.
  -h, --help  help for upload
  -t, --hint string    Hint associated with the password needed to decrypt the KeySecure Classic backup file.
  -u, --upload-id string   Used when resuming chunked uploads. May be specified when starting a chunked upload.
```

Ctx: ksctl policy > ksctl policy

Manage access control rules.

Ctx: ksctl policy > Synopsis

The policy commands can be used to perform CRUD operations with policies. Policies define a set of actions against a set of resources, and an effect, which is either allow or deny. Policies by themselves have no effect. You need to attach them to a principal. An attached policy references a policy, and a principal selector. Essentially, a principal can be specified via a set of key value pairs, e.g., Name equals Alice, Account equals Ford. Policy operations can be performed via 'ksctl policy xxx'. Policy attachments operations can be performed via 'ksctl polattach xxx'.

Ctx: ksctl policy create > ksctl policy create

Create a policy.

Ctx: ksctl policy create > Synopsis

The policy information is passed via a JSON file. The policy JSON file must contain the policy name. A boolean variable named allow specifies the effect of the policy, either to allow the actions or to deny the actions. The actions are specified by an array of strings which can contain the * wildcard character. The resources to which the policy applies are specified by an array of URI strings, which must be in URI format (::::). Any of the components of the URI may have a * wildcard character. The conditions under which the policy is applied is also specified by an array of strings. See the detailed documentation for further details related to the policy. The returned policy is displayed on the CLI. It contains the policy ID, URI, etc.

```
ksctl policy create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl policy create > Examples

```
  ksctl policy create --jsonfile abc.json
```

Ctx: ksctl policy create > Options

```
  -h, --help  help for create
  -j, --jsonfile string   Information for creating and updating policies is passed in JSON format via a file.
```

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs > ksctl records alarm-configs

Manage Alarm processing configuration.

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs > Synopsis

When a new record is created on a node it is compared against an alarm config condition. When a condition is satisfied, check for the threshold in given interval of time period (if threshold is set to non-zero) and if it meets, an alarm is triggered on the node with the name, description, and severity from the alarm config and the details from the record. Multiple alarms may be triggered by a single record.

The config condition is defined using Open Policy Agent's query language Rego, https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/how-do-i-write-policies/.

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs create > ksctl records alarm-configs create

Create a CipherTrust Manager alarm config on server records.

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs create > Synopsis

Create an alarm config that is tested against any new client record on the node to determine if an alarm should be triggered. Refer to the parent commands help for a more detailed description of how alarms are triggered from records.

The config condition is defined using Open Policy Agent's query language Rego. The following example triggers an alarm when all the subconditions are true.

    'input.clientType == "CTE"; input.event == "VMD Shut down"'

```
ksctl records alarm-configs create [flags]
```

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs create > Examples

```
  ksctl records alarm-configs create -n <name> -d <description> -e <severity> {-c <condition>|-f <file>} -t <number> -p <seconds>
  ksctl records alarm-configs create -n 'Weak RSA Key' -d 'An RSA key must be at least 2048 bits' -e critical -c 'input.success; input.message == "Create Key"; input.details.algorithm == "RSA"; input.details.size <= 1024' -t 10 -p 1000
  ksctl records alarm-configs create -n 'Weak RSA Key' -d 'An RSA key must be at least 2048 bits' -e critical -f condition.rego -t 10 -p 1000
```

Ctx: ksctl records alarm-configs create > Options

```
  -c, --condition string   A Rego query defined by Open Policy Agent. Separate subconditions by a ';'.
  -f, --conditionfile string   File with a Rego query defined by Open Policy Agent.
  -d, --description string  Description of alarm when triggered.
  -h, --help  help for create
  -p, --interval int  The interval is an integer value which defines the time interval in seconds and it is used for raising alarms if a threshold hits within this time interval.
  -n, --name string   Name of alarm when triggered (e.g. 'Weak RSA Key')
  -e, --severity string    Severity of alarm when triggered. See the REST API docs under Alarms for a list of severities.
  -t, --threshold int   The threshold is an integer value which defines the limit for raising alarm by observing the number of records fetched in given time interval. If it is not set then the default value will be 0 and it will not be used for raising alarm.
```

Ctx: ksctl scheduler > ksctl scheduler

Manage Scheduler Configuration and Jobs.

Ctx: ksctl scheduler > Synopsis

The CipherTrust Manager can periodically run key rotation, database backup, scp database backup and AWS External Key Store credential rotation jobs in the background.
These jobs can be configured using the scheduler.
Jobs can be scheduled by creating a job configuration (e.g. ksctl scheduler configs create key-rotation <args>).
Job configurations can be read, listed and deleted (ksctl scheduler configs get/list/delete <args>).
Job configurations can be updated (ksctl scheduler configs modify key-rotation <args>).
Jobs are run after job configurations are created.
The jobs that were run can be listed (ksctl scheduler jobs list <args>).

**Time Specification**

The time that a job runs is described in the run-at parameter using the cron expression format : "* * * * *".
These five values indicate when the job should be executed.
They are in order of minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.

The following table lists the accepted values:

Field Name   |   Mandatory?   |   Allowed Values    |   Allowed special characters
 ----------- |  ------------  |  -----------------  |  ----------------------------
Minute   |  Yes    |  0-59  | * / , -
Hour  |  Yes    |  0-23  | * / , -
Day of month |  Yes    |  1-31  | * / , - ?
Month    |  Yes    |  1-12 or JAN-DEC    | * / , -
Day of week  |  Yes    |  0-6 or SUN-SAT  | * / , - ?

- Month and Day of week field values are case insensitive.
  For example, "SUN", "Sun", and "sun" are equally accepted.

- Asterisk ( * ) The asterisk indicates that the cron expression will match for all values of the field;
  e.g., using an asterisk in the 5th field (month) would indicate every month.

- Slash ( / ) Slashes are used to describe increments of ranges.
  For example 3-59/15 in the 1st field (minutes) would indicate the 3rd minute of the hour
  and every 15 minutes thereafter.

- Comma ( , ) Commas are used to separate items of a list.
  For example, using "MON,WED,FRI" in the 5th field (day of week) would mean Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

- Hyphen ( - ) Hyphens are used to define ranges.
  For example, 9-17 would indicate every hour between 9am and 5pm inclusive,
  MON-WED would indicate Monday through Wednesday,
  JAN-JUN would indicate every month from January through June.

- Question mark ( ? ) Question mark can be used instead of ( * ) for leaving either day-of-month or day-of-week blank.
  ( ? ) means no specific value. For example, to run the job every 10th day of the month
  and not limit the job to a particular day of the week: "* * 10 * ?".

  --offset int  Specifies the offset time in seconds and is used to indicate the difference between the Creation Date and the
   Activation Date of the replacement key.
   -If no Offset is specified, the Activation Date,
   Process Start Date, Protect Stop Date and Deactivation Date values are copied from the
   existing key.
   -If Offset is set and dates exist for the existing key, then the dates of the
   replacement key are set based on the dates of the existing key by adding the offset such that:
   - Activation Date (RK) = Creation Date (RK) + Offset
   - Deactivation Date (RK) = Deactivation Date (EK) + (Difference of Activation Date of RK - Activation Date of EK),
   where RK represents the Replacement Key and EK is the Existing Key.

   For example, if a key is created at 2024-01-11T14:28:00 with an Activation Date specified as 2024-01-11T14:27:27. Now, if a request to replace this
   key is sent after five minutes i.e. at 2024-01-11T14:33:26 with an offset set to 600 secs (~10 mins.), then the

  "activationDate": string,
  "algorithm": string,
  "objectType": string ,
  "archiveDate": string,
  "curveid": string,
  "deactivationDate": string,
  "meta":
  { "ownerId": string }
  ,

    }

   'key=value[,key2=value2...]'.
  - A label's key has an optional prefix up to 253 characters followed by
  a forward slash and a required name up to 63 characters (e.g.
  'sales.widgets.com/region').
  - A label's value may be empty and may be up to 63 characters. Each
  part of the label (i.e. the prefix, name, and value) must begin and
  end with an alphanumeric character (a-zA-Z0-9).
  - Characters inbetween the beginning and end may contain alphanumeric
  characters, dots (.), dashes (-) and underscores (_).
  - Labels are merged when modifying an existing key or creating a new
  version. See --remove-labels to remove existing labels.
  - List matches keys that have the provided labels.

Ctx: ksctl tokens > ksctl tokens

Create and refresh JSON Web Tokens (JWT) that can be used to authenticate the CLI to a CipherTrust Manager device.

Ctx: ksctl tokens > Synopsis

The JWT (API authentication token / access token) that is created (or refreshed) can be used as an alternative to the user/password for access the proceted resources. The JWT can be used for authentication by setting the NCRYPTIFY_JWT configuration variable to the JWT that is output. Each JWT is created for a limited time. The JWT can be refreshed using the refresh token as input. If 'issue-refresh-token' flag is specified, a new refresh token is returned along with a new JWT. If both username/password and refresh token are specified, refresh token overrides username/password and is used to renew the JWT. Maximum lifetime (in minutes) for a refresh token can be specified using 'rt-life'. By default refresh tokens do not expire until revoked. Alternate way to cap lifetime of a refresh token is by setting an inactivity limit using 'rt-unused-life'. If set, the refresh token will be revoked if not used within the specified period (in minutes). By default 'rt-unused-life' policy is not enforced. If both 'rt-life' and 'rt-unused-life' are specified, 'rt-unused-life' should be less than 'rt-life'.
